methods.shareDays: Pro rata by day — total ÷ shares ÷ days
methods.presence: Pro rata by expense — expense ÷ day ÷ shares

methodHints.shares: The total spend is divided by the total number of shares, then multiplied by each person's shares. Dates play no part: someone there for two days pays as much as someone who stayed the whole trip, at equal shares. To account for a shorter stay, lower their shares. Example: 300 over 6 shares makes 50 a share, so someone holding 2 shares owes 100.
methodHints.shareDays: Each person weighs their shares multiplied by their days of presence. The total is divided by the sum of those share-days, which gives the price of one share for one day. Spending is therefore spread evenly across the stays: someone who left early still carries a fraction of what was spent after they went. Example: 10 days for one, 5 for the other, so 15 share-days; 300 makes 20 per share-day.
methodHints.presence: Each expense is handled on its own, on its own date. Only the people there that day share it, in proportion to their shares; the others carry none of it. A stay covers both its ends: the day someone leaves still counts, the day after does not. This is the truest to what happened, but it relies on expense dates being right. Example: someone who left on the 2nd pays half the groceries of the 2nd, and nothing of the dinner on the 8th.
